summary: Claims in batches timed from 2026-12-01T00:00Z on are judged under two new rules. A signature counts only within 7 days after it was made, by the time of the batch that carries it. The batch must keep its writer's order. A claim's ID covers its batch but its signature does not, so a writer could carry a validly signed claim's content again in a later batch: that copy is now invalid from its own fields once the original is old enough to be forgotten, on every member, whether or not it still holds the original. Until now the verdict of such a copy depended on whether a member had trimmed the original.

replay.detail: No replay and no scan. Batches before 2026-12-01T00:00Z are not checked. For later ones, judging a claim reads its batch's time and checks three index seeks: claims of the batch timed before it, the writer's previous batch, and batches its claims name as predecessors.

schema.detail: No table, index, column, kind, digest or storage version change. Constants in code: FRESHNESS_WINDOW_MS 7 days, FUTURE_SIGNATURE_MS 1 hour, FRESHNESS_FROM_UNIX_MS 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z.

rules.detail: For a claim whose batch is timed at or after 2026-12-01T00:00Z, three cases read Invalid. (1) The signature was made more than 7 days before the batch time: 'the signature is older than the freshness window'. (2) The signature is dated more than 1 hour after it: 'the signature is dated after its batch'. (3) The batch is out of its writer's order: a claim timed before its batch, or the batch timed before the writer's previous batch or before any batch its claims name as predecessors: 'its batch is timed before a batch it follows'. Measured on a real member over 3.2M signed claims: a batch's time is at most 12.4 s after its signatures (phone and browser requests) and up to 32.8 s before them (a node signs at seal). No claim is timed before its batch, no writer's batch times decrease, and no batch is timed before a predecessor's. So no honest claim measured is affected. A phone request signed more than 7 days before any node writes it must be signed again. The order check reads the writer's previous batch and its claims' predecessors' batches only where the member still holds them. Every member holds a batch younger than the forget bound (8 days), so for an active writer every member gives the same answer. Remaining gap, accepted: a writer whose previous batch is one some members no longer hold can still time a new batch within 7 days of an old signature and carry that claim's content again. Its previous batch would be one some members no longer hold if it is older than the forget bound, or if they joined from a checkpoint after it. A writer with no earlier batch and no predecessors can do the same. Members that forgot the original and members that hold it then judge the copy differently. It takes a member with a writer key.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest or capability change. Mixed versions: a build without the rule judges claims from 2026-12-01 on as before, so a replayed copy can read differently on old and new builds until every member runs this one. Builds with the rule agree wherever they hold the same batches the check reads, which every member does for an active writer. Authentication proofs (proof::authentication) apply the same rule from their verified records.

manual.detail: Nothing to do. Clocks should be roughly right: a writer whose clock is more than an hour behind a signer's makes that signature read as dated after its batch.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported; it judges these claims as before. Nothing is written.
